Q: Advice for transitioning into web development from a non-technical background A:

There really isn't any magic to learning any language. Just as you learned to operate a fork-lift safely, learned the basic rules, and then slowly got better through practice, practice, practice -- learning web development is no different. Others may have different thoughts, but with close to 25 years tinkering with it, what I would recommend is:

  • sticking to the basic tools, html, php (or your choice of server-side script) and javascript for client-side operations and CSS for styling,
  • avoid the massive library ecosystems (node.js, jquery, etc..) until you can recognize some specific benefit that your project needs from the library -- until then you are just spending time learning somebody else's collection of basic tools that may or may not remain supported in the future,
  • use a respected reference to answer any question you have about the specifics how any expression or object works, e.g. Mozilla's MDN, and to a basic extent W3Schools - they also each provide basic tutorials and examples how to use the various parts of each language (go through as many as you like/can),
  • don't forget to search StackOverflow, many, many of the questions that will come up have already been answered, and the context of the questions and answers here help fill in the areas not covered by tutorials and references,
  • decide on how you want your page or project to work, what information you want to present to and get from the user and how you want it to look -- before picking up the keyboard -- then write the code to accomplish that (yes, you will improve/change things along the way, but there is no substitute for knowing what you need to accomplish before you start pecking away),
  • pick tutorials and basic short example projects that are interesting to you, you are much more likely to dive into the learning that way rather than scanning pages while propping your eyes open with toothpicks,
  • pick the correct tool for the job. Know the difference between what is taking place client-side (in the browser) and what takes place server-side, and most important
  • enjoy what you are doing.

Web development, like learning anything else programming related, takes time to learn. Don't expect to be a wizard overnight. There are quite a few concepts you have to make friends with, especially that in web-programming a sizeable bit of it isn't simply sequential programming, but writing the code that will generate the content to be rendered by the browser on-the-fly (presenting a number of chicken-or-the-egg challenges). It's not just knowing the different parts and syntax of the various languages/tools, it's being able to write the code that lets them all work together to produce the result you want (securely).

Have fun and practice, practice, practice.

Q: What is the difference between readonly="true" & readonly="readonly"? A:

readonly="readonly" is xhtml syntax. In xhtml boolean attributes are written this way. In xhtml 'attribute minimization' (<input type="checkbox" checked>) isn't allowed, so this is the valid way to include boolean attributes in xhtml. See this page for more.information.

If your document type is xhtml transitional or strict and you want to validate it, use readonly="readonly" otherwise readonly is sufficient.

Q: Python Warning - Expected type 'Union[Integral, slice]', got 'str' instead A:

If variables/method returns are strongly typed these warnings go away.

Things like methods: def the_method(self, file_path: str) -> (list, list, int, int) and variables: list_a: list = [], the_number: int.

Q: How to get thread emails in a conversation by using GraphAPI A:

The issue is that once you have specified the receivedDateTime in $orderBy, you have to specify the receivedDateTime also in $filter, but before any other properties like

...$filter=receivedDateTime ge 1900-01-01 and conversationId%20eq%20'@{items('Apply_to_each_Email')['conversationId']}'...

https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/@{items('Apply_to_each_Email_Box')}/messages?$filter=receivedDateTime ge 1900-01-01 and conversationId%20eq%20'@{items('Apply_to_each_Email')['conversationId']}'&$top=5&$orderby=receivedDateTime%20desc&$select=id,subject,body,sender,from,toRecipients,ccRecipients,receivedDateTime,isRead

Check the documentation: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/user-list-messages?view=graph-rest-1.0&tabs=http#using-filter-and-orderby-in-the-same-query
